newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Athletics Australia executive director Neil King said given that Athletics was the biggest money-spinner from the Atlanta Olympics, AA may ask powerful International Amateur Athletic Federation president Primo Nebiolo to intervene in the fight against Federal Government budget cuts. Page 18.

Australian swimmer Michael Klim, 19, will compete in both the 100m butterfly and 200m freestyle in the national short-course swimming championships, despite the fact that both events run consecutively on the opening night. Klim will face a challenge in te pool from 17-year-old Geoff Huegill from Brisbane. Page 18.

Melbourne Tigers basketball player and Australian captain Andrew Gaze is likely to turn down an offer from a Greek basketball team which is said to be one of the better performing teams, because he wants to keep himself healthy for the 1998 world championhips, and hopefully the 2000 Sydney Olympics. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Sydney Swans AFL team looks set to re-sign Shannon Grant and Dale Lewis. New contracts should be signed this week, yet Grant will only sign for one year, with personal life in Sydney and homesickness for Melbourne, further prompted by an offer of a tree year contract by the Western Bulldogs' (formerly Footscray), complicating his choices. Page 41.

The Alice Springs Yacht Club's preparations for the Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race have been ongoing for 18 months, and involve 18 sailing enthusiasts from two crews flying spinnakers out of trees and practising tacking manoeuvres up a dry river bed. Page 41

While Australian Swimming Incorporated yesterday suspended a A$2,500 fine placed on breastroker Samantha Riley's coach Scott Volkers after Riley tested positive to the then-banned painkiller dextropropoxyphene, it upheld its findings against Volkers for the incident. Page 42.
THE AGE

Australian squash player Sarah FitzGerald, who returned to Melbourne this week, stunned herself by winning this year's world squash championships in Kuala Lumpur. Before the tournament, she had four wisdom teeth removed, then injured an ankle. FitzGerald then went on the defeat former world No.1, fellow Australian Michelle Martin, at the German Masters, which was the next tournament after the world championships. Page B6.

Carlton AFL player Mick McGuane's career hangs in the balance after he arrived drunk to a training session and became involved in a fight with rover Matthew Hogg. While McGuane has been fined around A$10,000, club officials insisted last night he would not be sacked. Page B8.

West Indian cricketer Brian Lara said yesterday he has felt the pressure of his poor performances on the Australian tour, knowing his team depended on him. Lara said, en route to Wangaratta to play against the Victorian team, that team morale had been lo, yet Tuesday's defeat of Pakistan had inspired hope. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian jockeys are considering striking over riding fees from Boxing Day unless they meet the Principal Racing Clubs early next week. The National Jockeys Council is pushing for a flat losing ride fee of A$130, which is comparative with that paid to most overseas riders. Page 101.

Melbourne Monarchs baseball team lefthander Damien Moss has been lost for the rest of the season, after suffering two fractures in his pitching hand. The loss of Moss, regarded as the next Australian player to play in the major leagues, is a blow to the Monarchs, who have not won a match in a month. Page 97.

Australian tennis player and former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash has criticised the playing surface for next month's Australian Tennis Open, saying it was a slow court designed for baseline players. Australian Open Tournament director Paul McNamee said yesterday Cash's assessment of the surface was premature. Page 96.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Former Australian Open singles finalist Kim Warwick said yesterday too many Australian tennis kids were soft in comparison to their US and European counterparts, and local talent must be developed rigorously if Australia intends to dominate tennis again. Page 87.

The New South Wales Interdistrict Athletics will be run this weekend, with Melinda Gainsford-Taylor, Veronica Lee and Rebecca Vormister - the Comeback Queens - likely to run. With three years away from athletics, 22-year-old Vormister was not planning torace this weekend, but upon hearing of the inclusion of Gainsford-Taylor and Lee, she is reconsidering. Page 80

New Australian Football League chief executive officer Wayne Jackson has raised the possibility of a second team for Sydney. Sydney Swans chairman Richard Colless believes a second team would benefit the city, yet Sydney Kings basketball team owner Mike Wrublewski is against the talk of a local rival. However, both teams agree that the talk is premature. Page 78.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
